topic.label: Claude Code Configuration
topic.desc: Claude Code Configuration: Settings, Permissions and sandboxing, Environments, Self-hosted environments, Model and responses, Interface.

concepts: Settings: Settings files and precedence, All settings, Example settings files.
Permissions and sandboxing: Configure permissions, Choose a permission mode, Auto mode classifier request charges, Configure the sandboxed Bash tool, Choose a sandbox environment.

Self-hosted environments: Self-hosted environments, Self-hosted environments quickstart, Deploy self-hosted environments to production, Customize sessions in self-hosted environments, Test self-hosted environments end to end, Self-hosted environments reference, Verify session identity in self-hosted environments.
Model and responses: Model configuration, Speed up responses with fast mode, Escalate hard decisions with the advisor tool, Output styles.
Interface: Configure your terminal for Claude Code, Fullscreen rendering, Use Claude Code with a screen reader, Voice dictation, Customize your status line, Customize keyboard shortcuts.
skills: Change Claude Code settings, pick the scope a key belongs in, verify the change, and learn which value Claude Code uses when a key is set in several places.
Reference for Claude Code settings.json keys: where each one goes, its type and default, and a paste-ready example, with an index of keys.
Realistic settings.json files for a developer, a team, and an organization: copy one, keep the keys you want, and change the values.
Control what Claude Code can access and do with fine-grained permission rules, modes, and managed policies.
Control whether Claude asks before acting. Switch permission modes with Shift+Tab in the CLI, the mode indicator in VS Code, or the mode selector in Desktop.
Resolve the Claude Code notice saying this session isn't eligible for auto mode's no-charge classifier requests: what it means, why it appears, and what to do.
Restrict the files and network hosts Claude Code's shell commands can reach with the built-in sandbox. Turn it on, set the boundary, and fix what it breaks.
Compare Claude Code sandbox options: the built-in sandboxed Bash tool, sandbox runtime, dev containers, Docker, and VMs. Choose the right isolation for your threat model.
Configure cloud environments for Claude Code cloud sessions: network access levels, environment variables, setup scripts, and environment caching.
Run Claude Code cloud sessions on infrastructure you control: set up a self-hosted environment, deploy runners, and route sessions to your own compute.
Set up your first self-hosted environment: install Claude Code, create the environment, start a runner, and route a session to it.
Run self-hosted runners in production: security hardening, network egress control, git credentials, Kubernetes and Compose recipes, and troubleshooting.
Customize self-hosted environment sessions with wrapper scripts for per-session credentials, lifecycle hooks, and on-demand runner spawning.
Test self-hosted environments end to end
Verify a self-hosted runner image from CI: dispatch a session with the CLI, read Claude's replies through a Stop hook, and script the full loop.
Reference for the self-hosted runner and orchestrator: CLI flags, environment variables, and Prometheus metrics.
Verify session identity in self-hosted environments
Verify the CLAUDECODESESSIONACCESSTOKEN JWT so services on your network can trust requests from sessions in your self-hosted environment.
Configure which model Claude Code uses, effort levels, extended context, and the auto-compact window
Speed up responses with fast mode
Get faster Opus and Fable responses in Claude Code by toggling fast mode with /fast.
Escalate hard decisions with the advisor tool
Pair your main model with a stronger advisor model that Claude consults at key moments during a task.
Change Claude Code's role, tone, and response format with a built-in output style such as Concise or Explanatory, or write a custom style.
Configure your terminal for Claude Code
Fix Shift+Enter for newlines, get a terminal bell when Claude finishes, configure tmux, match the color theme, and enable Vim mode in the Claude Code CLI.
Enable a smoother, flicker-free rendering mode with mouse support and stable memory usage in long conversations.
Use Claude Code with a screen reader
Set up Claude Code for screen readers such as VoiceOver and NVDA, plus settings for screen magnifiers, reduced motion, and colorblind-friendly themes.
Speak your prompts in the Claude Code CLI with hold-to-record or tap-to-record voice dictation.
Configure a custom status bar to monitor context window usage, costs, and git status in Claude Code
Customize keyboard shortcuts in Claude Code with a keybindings configuration file.

provenance.basis: Human0's claude_domain.csv (sha256 d26d41d8da4ed7dd622b6e6faa18a97dc91d4f3d2af972ae9715d41ee94963cc), converted by tools/claude_domain/build_claude_packs.py on 2026-11-27. Topics, concepts, skills (docs pages) and agent names are Human0's. A single-page skill's description is that page's own one-line description where the site publishes one (page_descriptions.json: llms.txt / llms-full.txt fetched 2026-11-27); concept descriptions, other skill descriptions, keywords, skill types (a verb rule), ids and the lexicon are generated from the CSV text.
provenance.mcp_notes: Human0's CSV lists 'Claude Developer Platform docs' for this topic, but that server (Claude Platform Docs, directory cc6f3470-080c-45b8-84e1-cdc03e9c6ac1) covers platform.claude.com only, by its own instructions, and a search for 'Claude Code hooks' on 2026-11-27 returned only platform.claude.com pages. No MCP server for these docs was verified, so the pack lists none.
provenance.limitations: Skills without a published page description (API reference endpoints and some guides) are described by their titles only; skill types come from the first word of the title. Docs pages change: the URLs were current in the CSV, not re-checked here.
